snp5.2:1.3: Why does it not become clear?
snp5.2:1.4: What do you say is its defilement?
snp5.2:2.1: “The world is enveloped by ignorance, Ajita, said the Fortunate One,
snp5.2:2.3: because of heedlessness and meanness it does not become clear.
snp5.2:2.4: Hunger is its defilement, I say; suffering is (the world’s) great fear.”
snp5.2:3.3: what is the constraint for streams?
snp5.2:3.4: Tell me the restraint for streams;
snp5.2:3.5: by what are the streams shut off?”
snp5.2:4.1: “Whatever streams there are in the world, Ajita, said the Fortunate One,
snp5.2:4.3: mindfulness is the constraint for them.
snp5.2:4.4: That is the restraint for streams, I say; by wisdom they are shut off.”
snp5.2:5.3: and mind and body, dear Sir,
snp5.2:5.4: please tell me this when asked:
snp5.2:6.1: “This question that was asked, Ajita, I can answer it!
snp5.2:6.3: As to where mind and body ceases without remainder:
snp5.2:7.2: and the many in training here,
snp5.2:7.3: when I ask the prudent one, please tell me their conduct, dear Sir.”
snp5.2:8.1: “He should not be greedy for sense pleasures,
snp5.2:8.3: Skilful in all things, the monk should wander mindfully.”
